Recursion State Rule:
Each recursive call represents its own state. Never overwrite the parent's state when exploring a child. Instead, compute a new child state and pass it to the recursive call.
Example:
• Parent: currentDepth = 2, maxDepth = 2
• Add '('
• Child: currentDepth = 3, maxDepth = 3
Pass (3, 3) to the child, but keep the parent as (2, 2).
For mutable objects (e.g., StringBuilder), undo changes after recursion. For primitive state (int), create new variables (newDepth, newMax) instead of modifying the parent's variables.
